fullText.simplified:
第五章、楚国的改革

    楚怀王让我负责改革工作。
    我很激动，努力工作，积极推进改革，一心想让百姓过上好生活。楚怀王十分信任我，不管是与官员开会，还是接见外国来的使者，他都带着我。遇到重要的事情，他也会问我的意见。我好像看到了一个强大而美好的楚国。
    四年后，楚国有了变化。百姓的生活在慢慢变好，国家也在慢慢变好。如果继续发展下去，楚国一定可以成为七国中最强大的国家。但是，楚国的贵族们不支持改革了。因为改革影响了他们的权势，他们不愿意变成没有权势的人。
    贵族们去楚怀王那儿说我的坏话。他们说我太骄傲了，说我不尊重楚怀王，说我的改革把楚国变得更乱了……楚怀王相信了吗？我不知道，我没有问过楚怀王。但我知道他受到了影响，他对我的态度变了，他不愿意见我，也不听我的意见了。
    这时候，北方的一个小国发生了一件大事，让楚怀王更不相信我了。
    这个小国是燕国。你还记得燕国吗？它是四个小国之一，在最北方。当时燕国也在进行改革，改革也影响了贵族的权势。贵族们一起反对改革，于是燕国发生了内乱。东边的齐国抓住这个机会，出兵攻打燕国。齐国的军队打进了燕国的王宫，杀死了燕王。
    改革引发这么严重的问题，这件事对楚怀王的影响特别大。他犹豫了，害怕了，不敢再继续了。他让我停止改革，然后拿走了我的工作，让我远离国家大事。
    失望和难过把我打倒了。我想去别的地方走走，于是离开了引都。
fullText.traditional:
第五章、楚國的改革

    楚懷王讓我負責改革工作。
    我很激動，努力工作，積極推進改革，一心想讓百姓過上好生活。楚懷王十分信任我，不管是與官員開會，還是接見外國來的使者，他都帶著我。遇到重要的事情，他也會問我的意見。我好像看到了一個強大而美好的楚國。
    四年後，楚國有了變化。百姓的生活在慢慢變好，國家也在慢慢變好。如果繼續發展下去，楚國一定可以成為七國中最強大的國家。但是，楚國的貴族們不支持改革了。因為改革影響了他們的權勢，他們不願意變成沒有權勢的人。
    貴族們去楚懷王那兒說我的壞話。他們說我太驕傲了，說我不尊重楚懷王，說我的改革把楚國變得更亂了……楚懷王相信了嗎？我不知道，我沒有問過楚懷王。但我知道他受到了影響，他對我的態度變了，他不願意見我，也不聽我的意見了。
    這時候，北方的一個小國發生了一件大事，讓楚懷王更不相信我了。
    這個小國是燕國。你還記得燕國嗎？它是四個小國之一，在最北方。當時燕國也在進行改革，改革也影響了貴族的權勢。貴族們一起反對改革，於是燕國發生了內亂。東邊的齊國抓住這個機會，出兵攻打燕國。齊國的軍隊打進了燕國的王宮，殺死了燕王。
    改革引發這麼嚴重的問題，這件事對楚懷王的影響特別大。他猶豫了，害怕了，不敢再繼續了。他讓我停止改革，然後拿走了我的工作，讓我遠離國家大事。
    失望和難過把我打倒了。我想去別的地方走走，於是離開了引都。

sentences.simplified: 楚怀王让我负责改革工作。
sentences.traditional: 楚懷王讓我負責改革工作。
sentences.pinyin: chǔ huái wáng ràng wǒ fù zé gǎi gé gōng zuò
sentences.english: King Huai of Chu put me in charge of the reform work.

sentences.simplified: 我很激动，努力工作，积极推进改革，一心想让百姓过上好生活。
sentences.traditional: 我很激動，努力工作，積極推進改革，一心想讓百姓過上好生活。
sentences.pinyin: wǒ hěn jī dòng nǔ lì gōng zuò jī jí tuī jìn gǎi gé yì xīn xiǎng ràng bǎi xìng guò shàng hǎo shēng huó
sentences.english: I was very excited, worked hard, actively drove the reforms forward, and was determined to improve the lives of the people.

sentences.simplified: 楚怀王十分信任我，不管是与官员开会，还是接见外国来的使者，他都带着我。
sentences.traditional: 楚懷王十分信任我，不管是與官員開會，還是接見外國來的使者，他都帶著我。
sentences.pinyin: chǔ huái wáng shí fēn xìn rèn wǒ bù guǎn shì yǔ guān yuán kāi huì hái shi jiē jiàn wài guó lái de shǐ zhě tā dōu dài zhe wǒ
sentences.english: King Huai of Chu trusted me greatly. Whether he was meeting with officials or receiving foreign envoys, he always took me along.

sentences.simplified: 遇到重要的事情，他也会问我的意见。
sentences.traditional: 遇到重要的事情，他也會問我的意見。
sentences.pinyin: yù dào zhòng yào de shì qing tā yě huì wèn wǒ de yì jiàn
sentences.english: When faced with important matters, he would also ask for my opinion.

sentences.simplified: 我好像看到了一个强大而美好的楚国。
sentences.traditional: 我好像看到了一個強大而美好的楚國。
sentences.pinyin: wǒ hǎo xiàng kàn dào le yí ge qiáng dà ér měi hǎo de chǔ guó
sentences.english: It felt as though I could already see a strong and flourishing Chu.

sentences.simplified: 四年后，楚国有了变化。
sentences.traditional: 四年後，楚國有了變化。
sentences.pinyin: sì nián hòu chǔ guó yǒu le biàn huà
sentences.english: Four years later, the state of Chu had changed.

sentences.simplified: 百姓的生活在慢慢变好，国家也在慢慢变好。
sentences.traditional: 百姓的生活在慢慢變好，國家也在慢慢變好。
sentences.pinyin: bǎi xìng de shēng huó zài màn man biàn hǎo guó jiā yě zài màn man biàn hǎo
sentences.english: The lives of the people were gradually improving, and the country was also gradually getting better.

sentences.simplified: 如果继续发展下去，楚国一定可以成为七国中最强大的国家。
sentences.traditional: 如果繼續發展下去，楚國一定可以成為七國中最強大的國家。
sentences.pinyin: rú guǒ jì xù fā zhǎn xià qù chǔ guó yí dìng kě yǐ chéng wéi qī guó zhōng zuì qiáng dà de guó jiā
sentences.english: If this development continued, the state of Chu could certainly become the strongest of the Seven Warring States.

sentences.simplified: 但是，楚国的贵族们不支持改革了。
sentences.traditional: 但是，楚國的貴族們不支持改革了。
sentences.pinyin: dàn shì chǔ guó de guì zú men bù zhī chí gǎi gé le
sentences.english: However, the nobles of the state of Chu no longer supported the reforms.

sentences.simplified: 因为改革影响了他们的权势，他们不愿意变成没有权势的人。
sentences.traditional: 因為改革影響了他們的權勢，他們不願意變成沒有權勢的人。
sentences.pinyin: yīn wèi gǎi gé yǐng xiǎng le tā men de quán shì tā men bú yuàn yì biàn chéng méi yǒu quán shì de rén
sentences.english: Since the changes affected their power and influence, they were unwilling to become people without power and influence.

sentences.simplified: 贵族们去楚怀王那儿说我的坏话。
sentences.traditional: 貴族們去楚懷王那兒說我的壞話。
sentences.pinyin: guì zú men qù chǔ huái wáng nà'r shuō wǒ de huài huà
sentences.english: The nobles went to King Huai of Chu and spoke ill of me.

sentences.simplified: 他们说我太骄傲了，说我不尊重楚怀王，说我的改革把楚国变得更乱了……
sentences.traditional: 他們說我太驕傲了，說我不尊重楚懷王，說我的改革把楚國變得更亂了……
sentences.pinyin: tā men shuō wǒ tài jiāo ào le shuō wǒ bù zūn zhòng chǔ huái wáng shuō wǒ de gǎi gé bǎ chǔ guó biàn de gèng luàn le
sentences.english: They said I was too arrogant, that I disrespected King Huai of Chu, and that my reforms had made the state of Chu even more chaotic.

sentences.simplified: 楚怀王相信了吗？我不知道，我没有问过楚怀王。
sentences.traditional: 楚懷王相信了嗎？我不知道，我沒有問過楚懷王。
sentences.pinyin: chǔ huái wáng xiāng xìn le ma wǒ bù zhī dào wǒ méi yǒu wèn guò chǔ huái wáng
sentences.english: Did King Huai of Chu believe them? I don’t know. I never asked him.

sentences.simplified: 但我知道他受到了影响，
sentences.traditional: 但我知道他受到了影響，
sentences.pinyin: dàn wǒ zhī dào tā shòu dào le yǐng xiǎng
sentences.english: But I know he was influenced by them.

sentences.simplified: 他对我的态度变了，他不愿意见我，也不听我的意见了。
sentences.traditional: 他對我的態度變了，他不願意見我，也不聽我的意見了。
sentences.pinyin: tā duì wǒ de tài dù biàn le tā bú yuàn yì jiàn wǒ yě bù tīng wǒ de yì jiàn le
sentences.english: His attitude towards me changed; he was unwilling to see me, and he no longer listened to my opinions.

sentences.simplified: 这时候，北方的一个小国发生了一件大事，让楚怀王更不相信我了。
sentences.traditional: 這時候，北方的一個小國發生了一件大事，讓楚懷王更不相信我了。
sentences.pinyin: zhè shí hou běi fāng de yí ge xiǎo guó fā shēng le yí jiàn dà shì ràng chǔ huái wáng gèng bù xiāng xìn wǒ le
sentences.english: At this time, a major event occurred in a small northern state, which made King Huai of Chu trust me even less.

sentences.simplified: 这个小国是燕国。你还记得燕国吗？它是四个小国之一，在最北方。
sentences.traditional: 這個小國是燕國。你還記得燕國嗎？它是四個小國之一，在最北方。
sentences.pinyin: zhè ge xiǎo guó shì yān guó nǐ hái jì de yān guó ma tā shì sì ge xiǎo guó zhī yī zài zuì běi fāng
sentences.english: This small state was Yan. Do you remember Yan? It was one of the four small states, located in the far north.

sentences.simplified: 当时燕国也在进行改革，改革也影响了贵族的权势。
sentences.traditional: 當時燕國也在進行改革，改革也影響了貴族的權勢。
sentences.pinyin: dāng shí yān guó yě zài jìn xíng gǎi gé gǎi gé yě yǐng xiǎng le guì zú de quán shì
sentences.english: At that time, Yan was also undergoing reforms. These reforms also affected the power of the nobles.

sentences.simplified: 贵族们一起反对改革，于是燕国发生了内乱。
sentences.traditional: 貴族們一起反對改革，於是燕國發生了內亂。
sentences.pinyin: guì zú men yì qǐ fǎn duì gǎi gé yú shì yān guó fā shēng le nèi luàn
sentences.english: The nobles collectively opposed the reforms, leading to internal turmoil in Yan.

sentences.simplified: 东边的齐国抓住这个机会，出兵攻打燕国。
sentences.traditional: 東邊的齊國抓住這個機會，出兵攻打燕國。
sentences.pinyin: dōng bian de qí guó zhuā zhù zhè ge jī huì chū bīng gōng dǎ yān guó
sentences.english: The eastern state of Qi seized this opportunity and sent troops to attack Yan.

sentences.simplified: 齐国的军队打进了燕国的王宫，杀死了燕王。
sentences.traditional: 齊國的軍隊打進了燕國的王宮，殺死了燕王。
sentences.pinyin: qí guó de jūn duì dǎ jìn le yān guó de wáng gōng shā sǐ le yān wáng
sentences.english: Qi’s army invaded the Yan royal palace and killed the King of Yan.

sentences.simplified: 改革引发这么严重的问题，这件事对楚怀王的影响特别大。
sentences.traditional: 改革引發這麼嚴重的問題，這件事對楚懷王的影響特別大。
sentences.pinyin: gǎi gé yǐn fā zhè me yán zhòng de wèn tí zhè jiàn shì duì chǔ huái wáng de yǐng xiǎng tè bié dà
sentences.english: The reforms had caused such severe problems, and this incident had a significant impact on King Huai of Chu.

sentences.simplified: 他犹豫了，害怕了，不敢再继续了。
sentences.traditional: 他猶豫了，害怕了，不敢再繼續了。
sentences.pinyin: tā yóu yù le hài pà le bù gǎn zài jì xù le
sentences.english: He hesitated, became fearful, and dared not continue.

sentences.simplified: 他让我停止改革，然后拿走了我的工作，让我远离国家大事。
sentences.traditional: 他讓我停止改革，然後拿走了我的工作，讓我遠離國家大事。
sentences.pinyin: tā ràng wǒ tíng zhǐ gǎi gé rán hòu ná zǒu le wǒ de gōng zuò ràng wǒ yuǎn lí guó jiā dà shì
sentences.english: He asked me to stop the reforms, then took away my position, distancing me from state affairs.

sentences.simplified: 失望和难过把我打倒了。我想去别的地方走走，于是离开了引都。
sentences.traditional: 失望和難過把我打倒了。我想去別的地方走走，於是離開了引都。
sentences.pinyin: shī wàng hé nán guò bǎ wǒ dǎ dǎo le wǒ xiǎng qù bié de dì fang zǒu zǒu yú shì lí kāi le yǐn dū
sentences.english: Disappointment and sadness overwhelmed me. I wanted to go somewhere else, so I left Yindu.

sentence_translations: Chapter 5: Reforming the State of Chu
King Huai of Chu put me in charge of the reform work.
I was very excited, worked hard, actively drove the reforms forward, and was determined to improve the lives of the people.
King Huai of Chu trusted me greatly. Whether he was meeting with officials or receiving foreign envoys, he always took me along.
When faced with important matters, he would also ask for my opinion.
It felt as though I could already see a strong and flourishing Chu.
Four years later, the state of Chu had changed.
The lives of the people were gradually improving, and the country was also gradually getting better.
If this development continued, the state of Chu could certainly become the strongest of the Seven Warring States.
However, the nobles of the state of Chu no longer supported the reforms.
Since the changes affected their power and influence, they were unwilling to become people without power and influence.
The nobles went to King Huai of Chu and spoke ill of me.
They said I was too arrogant, that I disrespected King Huai of Chu, and that my reforms had made the state of Chu even more chaotic.
Did King Huai of Chu believe them? I don’t know. I never asked him.
But I know he was influenced by them.
His attitude towards me changed; he was unwilling to see me, and he no longer listened to my opinions.
At this time, a major event occurred in a small northern state, which made King Huai of Chu trust me even less.
This small state was Yan. Do you remember Yan? It was one of the four small states, located in the far north.
At that time, Yan was also undergoing reforms. These reforms also affected the power of the nobles.
The nobles collectively opposed the reforms, leading to internal turmoil in Yan.
The eastern state of Qi seized this opportunity and sent troops to attack Yan.
Qi’s army invaded the Yan royal palace and killed the King of Yan.
The reforms had caused such severe problems, and this incident had a significant impact on King Huai of Chu.
He hesitated, became fearful, and dared not continue.
He asked me to stop the reforms, then took away my position, distancing me from state affairs.
Disappointment and sadness overwhelmed me. I wanted to go somewhere else, so I left Yindu.
